(Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) | college = [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] (2004–2008) | draft_year = 2008 | career_start = 2008 | career_end = 2013 | career_number = 31 | career_position = [[Small forward]] | years1 = {{nbay|2008|full=y}} | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = 2009–2010 | team2 = [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] | years3 = 2010–2011 | team3 = [[CB Granada|Granada]] | years4 = 2011 | team4 = [[Artland Dragons]] | years5 = 2011–2012 | team5 = [[UCAM Murcia CB|Murcia]] | years6 = 2012 | team6 = [[SLUC Nancy]] | years7 = 2012–2013 | team7 = [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] | highlights = * [[NBA D-League All Star]] ([[2009–10 NBA Development League season|2010]]) * [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Second Team]] ([[2009–10 NBA Development League season|2010]]) }} '''Robert Karl Kurz''' (born March 5, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played one season in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Golden State Warriors]], and later played in the top leagues in Spain, Germany, and France. ==High school== Kurz transferred to [[Penn Charter]] following two years at [[Germantown Academy]]. In his junior year at Penn Charter, Kurz averaged 18.0 points and 12.0 rebounds per game. As a senior, he averaged 18.5 points and 12.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Rob Kurz Profile|url=https://und.com/roster/rob-kurz|work=UND.com|accessdate=30 October 2020}} ==College career== In his freshman season at the [[University of Notre Dame]], Kurz appeared in fourteen games and averaged 1.4 points and 1.1 rebounds per game. He recorded career bests of 11 points and 7 rebounds in a [[National Invitation Tournament]] first-round loss to [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]]. In his sophomore season, Kurz averaged 6.4 points and 5.1 rebounds per game, appearing in all thirty games. Kurz was named to the [[Big East]] Weekly Honor Roll on November 21 after recording 18 points in Notre Dame's season opener. Kurz was one of the three captains for Notre Dame his junior season. He averaged 12.6 points and 8.0 rebounds per game during the season. On December 4, 2006, Kurz was named to the Big East Weekly Honor Roll for the second time in his career after averaging 19.6 points and 7.7 rebounds per game in wins over [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Lehigh]], [[Winston-Salem State Rams men's basketball|Winston-Salem]], and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]. Kurz served as a team captain for the second consecutive season, and was also the only [[senior (education)|senior]] on Notre Dame's roster. He started in all thirty-three games and averaged 12.8 points and 7.1 rebounds per game. Kurz led Notre Dame with 48 blocks, finishing with 122 blocked shots in his career, which ranks sixth all-time for Notre Dame. On December 31, 2007, he was named to the Big East Weekly Honor Roll for the third time in his career. ==Professional career== Kurz played with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[NBA Summer League]] prior to the [[2008–09 NBA season]]. In 11 games, Kurz averaged 7.1 points and 4.5 rebounds per game. He also played four games with the Warriors at the [[Rocky Mountain Revue]], where he averaged 12.5 points and 6.8 rebounds per game. On September 9, 2008, Kurz signed a contract with the Warriors.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Nelson, Dowell and Kurz|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_dowell_kurz_nelson.html|work=nba.com|accessdate=10 July 2012}} On April 11, 2009, Kurz tallied a career-high 21 points against the [[2008–09 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Golden State Warriors vs. Utah Jazz recap|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290411026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211130184648/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290411026|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 30, 2021|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=10 July 2012}} Kurz agreed to a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on August 15, 2009. On October 19, Kurz was waived by the Cavaliers. He played in five games during the preseason, averaging 3.4 points and 2.0 rebounds in 9.8 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2009/10/cleveland_cavaliers_waive_kurz.html|title=Cleveland Cavaliers waive Kurz, Neville|first=Plain|last=Dealer|date=20 October 2009|website=cleveland.com|accessdate=30 April 2019}} From 2009 to 2010 Kurz played 39 games for the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA D-League]], averaging 17.5 ppg and 10.1 rpg.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Rob-Kurz/D-League/953/2010/By_Season/Per_Game/Regular_Season|title=Rob Kurz D-League profile|author=|date=|publisher=|accessdate=30 October 2020}} Kurz was signed by the [[Chicago Bulls]] on April 9, 2010,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5070904|title=Bulls waive C James; sign F Kurz from NBDL|author=|date=9 April 2010|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=30 October 2020}} but never played for the team and was waived on June 30.[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/67614/20100630/bulls_waive_kurz_richard_to_create_more_cap_space/ Bulls Waive Kurz, Richard To Create More Cap Space] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100703135304/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/67614/20100630/bulls_waive_kurz_richard_to_create_more_cap_space |date=2010-07-03 }} In August 2010, Kurz signed with the Spanish club [[CB Granada]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/12143/cb_granada_tabs_rob_kurz.html|title=CB Granada tabs Rob Kurz|author=|date=|publisher=|accessdate=30 April 2019}} In January 2011, Kurz signed with the German club [[Artland Dragons]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/germany/21329/rob_kurz_officially_moves_to_artland_dragons.html|title=sportando.net|author=|date=|publisher=|accessdate=30 April 2019}} He returned to [[Spain]] in July 2011 by signing with [[CB Murcia]] for one season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/29835/ucam_murcia_lands_robert_kurz.html|title=UCAM Murcia lands Robert Kurz|author=|date=|publisher=|accessdate=30 April 2019}} In February 2012, Kurz signed with the French club [[SLUC Nancy]]. Prior to the [[2012–13 NBA season]], Kurz agreed to play with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=2012 NBA Summer League rosters|url=http://nbadraft.net/2012-nba-summer-league-rosters|work=draftnet.com|accessdate=10 July 2012}} In September 2012, Kurz and [[Micah Downs]] joined the [[Boston Celtics]] as training camp invitees,{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/celtics-sign-downs-and-kurz|title=Celtics Sign Downs and Kurz|author=|date=|website=Boston Celtics|accessdate=30 April 2019}} but neither player made the team's final roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-waive-downs-kurz|title=Celtics Waive Downs, Kurz|author=|date=|website=Boston
